context: For the height array ht = [3, 8, 5, 2, 7, 7, 3, 4], indexed from 0 to 7, container capacity is cap[i, j] = min(ht[i], ht[j]) × (j - i).

The greedy algorithm starts with the left pointer i = 0, the right pointer j = 7, and the maximum so far res = 0. While i < j, first compute the current capacity cap and update the maximum with res = max(res, cap). Then compare the board heights and move the pointer at the shorter board one position inward. Exit the loop when i and j meet.
description: The sequence has 9 steps. A teal i and a blue j above the selected boards mark the left and right pointers. Each board is highlighted in its pointer's color. Steps 2 through 8 shade the current container light blue and show below it how to compute cap and update the maximum so far, res.

Step 1 initializes the pointers, steps 2 through 8 perform seven capacity calculations, and step 9 exits when the pointers meet. The player step number therefore differs from the calculation count. The table “Maximum capacity, steps 2–8: calculations and running maximum” after the list summarizes the values by step. The diagrams label the pointers, cap, and res. The board heights can be read from the axis.

frames.announcement: Start the two pointers at opposite ends of the array, i = 0 and j = 7. Set the maximum capacity so far to res = 0.
frames.explanation: Set the left pointer to i = 0 at the leftmost board of height 3 and the right pointer to j = 7 at the rightmost board of height 4. Set the maximum capacity so far to res = 0. The first capacity calculation has yet to begin, and the figure does not yet show a water-filled area.
frames.key_state: Initially, i = 0 (height 3), j = 7 (height 4), and the maximum so far is res = 0. The current capacity has yet to be calculated.
frames.title: Initialize the pointers at opposite ends

frames.announcement: Evaluate the two ends. The left board (height 3) is shorter than the right (height 4). The capacity is cap = 21, so update res to 21.
frames.explanation: The first calculation uses the two ends, [0, 7]. The left height is ht[0] = 3 and the right height is ht[7] = 4. The width is 7 - 0 = 7, so the current capacity is cap = min(3, 4) × 7 = 21. Update the maximum to res = max(0, 21) = 21. The left board (3) is shorter than the right (4), so move i to the right next.
frames.key_state: At i = 0 (height 3) and j = 7 (height 4), the left board is shorter. Width 7, water height 3, current capacity cap = 21, maximum so far res = 21.
frames.title: Calculate the capacity between boards [0, 7]

frames.announcement: Move the left pointer right from 0 to 1. The right board (height 4) is shorter than the left (height 8). The capacity is cap = 24, so update res to 24.
frames.explanation: The left board was shorter, so move i right from 0 to 1 to reach [1, 7]. The left height is ht[1] = 8, the right height is ht[7] = 4, and the width is 7 - 1 = 6. The current capacity is cap = min(8, 4) × 6 = 24. Update the maximum to res = max(21, 24) = 24. The right board (4) is now shorter than the left (8), so move j to the left next.
frames.key_state: At i = 1 (height 8) and j = 7 (height 4), the right board is shorter. Width 6, water height 4, current capacity cap = 24, maximum so far res = 24.
frames.title: Move the pointer at the shorter board right to i = 1

frames.announcement: Move the right pointer left from 7 to 6. The right board (height 3) is shorter than the left (height 8). The capacity is cap = 15, so res stays at 24.
frames.explanation: The previous right board (height 4) was shorter than the left (height 8), so move j left from 7 to 6, reaching [1, 6]. The left height is 8, the right height is ht[6] = 3, and the width is 6 - 1 = 5. The current capacity is cap = min(8, 3) × 5 = 15. The maximum so far stays at res = max(24, 15) = 24.
frames.key_state: At i = 1 (height 8) and j = 6 (height 3), the right board is shorter. Width 5, water height 3, current capacity cap = 15, maximum so far res = 24.
frames.title: Move the pointer at the shorter board left to j = 6

frames.announcement: Move the right pointer left from 6 to 5. The right board (height 7) is shorter than the left (height 8). The capacity is cap = 28, so update res to 28.
frames.explanation: The previous right board (height 3) was shorter than the left (height 8), so move j left from 6 to 5, reaching [1, 5]. The left height is 8, the right height is ht[5] = 7, and the width is 5 - 1 = 4. The current capacity is cap = min(8, 7) × 4 = 28. The maximum so far rises to res = max(24, 28) = 28.
frames.key_state: At i = 1 (height 8) and j = 5 (height 7), the right board is shorter. Width 4, water height 7, current capacity cap = 28, maximum so far res = 28.
frames.title: Move the pointer at the shorter board left to j = 5

frames.announcement: Move the right pointer left from 5 to 4. The right board (height 7) is shorter than the left (height 8). The capacity is cap = 21, so res stays at 28.
frames.explanation: The previous right board (height 7) was shorter than the left (height 8), so move j left from 5 to 4, reaching [1, 4]. The left height is 8, the right height is ht[4] = 7, and the width is 4 - 1 = 3. The current capacity is cap = min(8, 7) × 3 = 21. The maximum so far stays at res = max(28, 21) = 28.
frames.key_state: At i = 1 (height 8) and j = 4 (height 7), the right board is shorter. Width 3, water height 7, current capacity cap = 21, maximum so far res = 28.
frames.title: Move the pointer at the shorter board left to j = 4

frames.announcement: Move the right pointer left from 4 to 3. The right board (height 2) is shorter than the left (height 8). The capacity is cap = 4, so res stays at 28.
frames.explanation: The previous right board (height 7) was shorter than the left (height 8), so move j left from 4 to 3, reaching [1, 3]. The left height is 8, the right height is ht[3] = 2, and the width is 3 - 1 = 2. The current capacity is cap = min(8, 2) × 2 = 4. The maximum so far stays at res = max(28, 4) = 28.
frames.key_state: At i = 1 (height 8) and j = 3 (height 2), the right board is shorter. Width 2, water height 2, current capacity cap = 4, maximum so far res = 28.
frames.title: Move the pointer at the shorter board left to j = 3

frames.announcement: Move the right pointer left from 3 to 2. The right board (height 5) is shorter than the left (height 8). The capacity is cap = 5, so res stays at 28.
frames.explanation: The previous right board (height 2) was shorter than the left (height 8), so move j left from 3 to 2, reaching [1, 2]. The left height is 8, the right height is ht[2] = 5, and the width is 2 - 1 = 1. The current capacity is cap = min(8, 5) × 1 = 5. The maximum so far stays at res = max(28, 5) = 28.
frames.key_state: At i = 1 (height 8) and j = 2 (height 5), the right board is shorter. Width 1, water height 5, current capacity cap = 5, maximum so far res = 28.
frames.title: Move the pointer at the shorter board left to j = 2

frames.announcement: The right pointer moves left to index 1 and meets the left pointer. Exit the loop and return the maximum capacity of 28.
frames.explanation: The right board (height 5) was shorter than the left board (height 8), so move j left from index 2 to index 1, where it meets i. The teal i and blue j now appear together above the board at index 1. The number 2 on the horizontal axis is now dark gray, like the other unselected indices. Since i < j is now false, exit the loop without calculating another capacity and return the maximum, res = 28.
frames.key_state: The pointers meet at i = j = 1. Exit the greedy loop and return the maximum capacity, res = 28.
frames.title: The pointers meet: return the maximum capacity

summary: Start a pointer at each end and move the one at the shorter board inward. Compute the current capacity and track the largest seen at each step. The result is 28.
